column1: # client-go source evidence for Campaign 16 BatchCommands wire and in-flight ownership.

column5: One route-generation-scoped in-flight table owns cancellation and exactly-once completion for async batch entries. A real tonic duplex stream, reconnect loop, production timeouts, and live TiKV validation remain external.

The scheduler moves each original completion into one generation-keyed pending table, rejects duplicate or zero IDs, isolates forwarded routes, and retires terminal entries once. Duplex stream creation, packet loops, reconnect, metrics, and live transport remain external.

Route and stream generation are explicit in the sole in-flight authority so a stale stream cannot retire replacement IDs. Real tonic stream ownership, connection lifecycle, and reconnect remain external.

Opaque immutable request bodies preserve pinned BatchCommands oneof tags and typed response demultiplexing without inventing unsupported command payloads. The remaining command switch, concrete protobuf bodies, streaming transport, and live TiKV parity remain open.
